cards.text: Friend, today we're reading somebody else's mail, and for once nobody's gonna yell at me for it. This letter is from Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, and Timothy, who Paul calls our brother. It's going to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says he's an apostle of Christ Jesus because the other apostles picked him.

cards.text: Paul opens with grace and peace to them from God our Father. Then he tells them what he and Timothy always do when they pray for them.

cards.question: When Paul and Timothy pray for the Colossians, they always ___ God.
Paul and Timothy are thankful because of what they've heard about the Colossians: their ___ in Christ Jesus and their ___ for all the saints.

cards.text: Paul says that faith and love come from a hope that's stored up for the Colossians. Stored up, like the chocolate chips I hide from myself on the top shelf, which NEVER works, because baker, this mustache has REACH.

cards.question: Paul says the Colossians' faith and love come from a hope stored up for them. Where is that hope stored?

cards.text: They first heard about that hope in the word of truth, the gospel. And Paul says the gospel isn't just sitting on the counter cooling off.

cards.question: The gospel has come to the Colossians. What does Paul say it's doing all over the world?
True or false: Paul says the gospel has been bearing fruit among the Colossians too, ever since the day they heard it and truly understood the grace of God.
Somebody taught the gospel to the Colossians. Who did they learn it from?

cards.text: That's Epaphras, and Paul calls him "our beloved fellow servant" and a faithful minister of Christ. BELOVED, baker, and the last thing anybody called me in that kitchen was "Where'd the stamper go?"

cards.question: Epaphras also told Paul and Timothy about the Colossians. What did he tell them about?

cards.text: Paul has told the Colossians why he and Timothy thank God for them. Now he tells them what they keep asking God for. Since the day they heard about the Colossians, they have not STOPPED praying for them, and baker, I can't even keep an oven timer going that long.

cards.question: What do Paul and Timothy keep asking God to fill the Colossians with?
Paul wants the Colossians filled with the knowledge of God's will. What's it for?

answers.text: So they may walk worthy of the Lord
So they may win every argument
So they may earn God's love

cards.text: Notice this, baker: earlier the gospel was bearing fruit and growing, and now Paul prays the Colossians will be bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God. Same dough, new batch, and the batch is THEM.

cards.question: True or false: Paul prays the Colossians will please the Lord in a few important ways.

cards.text: Next Paul prays they'll be strengthened with all power, according to God's glorious might. ALL power, baker, and I need a sit-down after stamping one tray.

cards.question: Paul prays the Colossians will be strengthened with all power. What's all that strength for?
Paul wants the Colossians strong and patient. What else does he want them doing, joyfully?

cards.text: And Paul tells them why there's so much to be thankful for. It's because of what the Father has done for them.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the Colossians had to qualify themselves to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light.

cards.text: Then Paul tells what the Father has done for us. And baker, give me a second, because this one hits close to home.

cards.question: Paul says the Father has rescued us from the dominion of ___.

cards.text: Rescued from the dark and brought into the kingdom of His beloved Son, Jesus. I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, baker, so don't mind me, I'm just over here crying into my apron.

cards.question: In the Son we have redemption, the ___ of sins.

findings.problem: The answer to this true or false is that Paul is an apostle 'by the will of God' (Col 1:1). No card ever says that. Card 1 leaves it out, and the false statement only rules out 'the other apostles picked him.' The baker has no context to reason from, so this is a coin flip, and they leave Prep without the key detail of where Paul's apostleship comes from.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The joke compares the hope 'stored up for you in heaven' (Col 1:5) to chocolate chips he hides from himself, and the punchline is that the hiding never works. That suggests stored-up things don't stay stored, which works against the point of the verse: the hope is kept safe for them. The action in the comparison (hiding something from yourself and failing) is not the action in the text (something kept safe and waiting for its owner).

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup line 'the gospel isn't just sitting on the counter cooling off' rules out both wrong answers on card 9. 'Waiting to be preached' is the same as just sitting. 'Slowing down and fading' is the same as cooling off. Only the right answer is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke invents a moment in the Millers' kitchen: someone asking 'Where'd the stamper go?' In the backstory, Mother Miller deliberately picked him up and slid him into the drawer, and nobody looked for him. The line adds to his backstory and contradicts it. It also doesn't click: 'Where'd the stamper go?' isn't something anyone 'called' him, so the contrast with 'beloved' needs explaining.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card of the passage may have 3. The first sentence ('Paul has told the Colossians why he and Timothy thank God for them.') is also a recap of stop 1 and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Strength for every battle' is close to something Paul does pray for in this passage: that they be 'strengthened with all power' (Col 1:11). A baker could argue it's right. It needs to be false anywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
